history.dynasty: Yadava / Hemadpanti (main temple, 13th century); Peshwa-period repairs; Ahilyabai Holkar renovation
history.period: 13th century origins; sub-shrines from various later additions
history.summary: This record covers the subsidiary shrines of the Aundha Nagnath Temple complex at Aundha Nagnath (Hingoli district) - one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Shiva, traditionally held to be the first. The Maharashtra Tourism department and travel sources describe the complex as housing twelve mini-shrines symbolically dedicated to the other Jyotirlingas, plus about 108 smaller temples and 68 sub-shrines clustered around the main sanctum, including shrines to Parvati, Ganesha, Kartikeya, Nandi, Dattatreya, Nilakanteshwar, the Dashavatara and Veda Vyasa, and a Shani temple near the Sash Kund and Bahu Kund water tanks. The main temple itself is a 13th-century Yadava/Hemadpanti stone structure (underground garbhagriha, south-facing entrance), damaged during Mughal-era invasions - one legend credits a swarm of bees with driving off Aurangzeb's men - and rebuilt/renovated by Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar, whose statue stands at the entrance. NOTE: this is a component record of the larger Nagnath complex (CSV town 'Aundha Nagnath' is correct; it is in Hingoli district, not Aurangabad district). Counts of 12/108/68 shrines are from travel sources and should be treated as approximate (verify).

name: Subsidiary Jyotirlinga Shrines, Nagnath Temple Complex
town_description: Aundha Nagnath is a temple town on the Hingoli-Parbhani road in Hingoli district of Maharashtra's Marathwada region, named for its Jyotirlinga shrine to Nagnath (a form of Shiva associated with serpents). It is an important pilgrimage stop on the Maharashtra Jyotirlinga circuit, commonly combined with Parli Vaijnath about 110-120 km away. The town is small and rural, with the hill-set temple complex and its stone tanks dominating local life.

travel.airport: Nanded Airport (Shri Guru Gobind Singh Ji Airport), approx. 70-80 km (verify); Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) Airport is approx. 200 km+ (verify).
travel.railway: Chondi is the nearest railhead per travel sources (verify); Hingoli Junction and Parbhani Junction are other options with buses/autos onward.
travel.road: On the Hingoli-Parbhani road; MSRTC and private buses run from Nanded, Parbhani, Hingoli and Chondi. The temple is reached by steps up the hill from Aundha village.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for cool weather; Maha Shivaratri and the Magha-Falgun fair are the most significant but most crowded times.
visitor_information.opening_hours: The complex is generally open approx. 4:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily (verify - figures come from the main temple's timings and may not reflect every sub-shrine).
